source.title: Family traditions and seasonal decorations written for Prospero Dungeon
source.note: General knowledge of how families keep holidays. A tradition names a holiday by its id in holidays.json and the calendars it fits.

dishes: sweet potato casserole with marshmallows on top
a turkey that takes all morning
green bean casserole with the crispy onions
pecan pie and pumpkin pie, both
macaroni and cheese baked in the big dish
cranberry sauce still in the shape of the can
collard greens that simmer all day
rituals: Everyone goes around the table saying one thing they are thankful for.
The football game is on with the sound low and nobody admits to watching it.
Leftovers go home in a stack of mismatched containers.
There is a walk around the block between dinner and pie.
The kids table never quite goes away, whatever age you are.
The wishbone gets saved to dry on the windowsill.

dishes: seven fishes, or as close as anyone gets
hot chocolate with too many marshmallows
a cheese board that is really dinner
rituals: Everyone opens one present, always new pajamas.
A Christmas Eve movie, the same one every year.
A drive around the neighborhood to look at the lights.
Midnight service, or at least the early one.

dishes: prime rib saved for this one day
a breakfast casserole made the night before
sugar cookies left over from decorating
eggnog that someone made from scratch
rituals: Stockings come before anything else.
Presents get opened one at a time so everyone can watch.
A long afternoon of board games that gets competitive.
A phone call to the relatives who could not come.
Wrapping paper fights once the presents are open.

dishes: a tray of pigs in a blanket
black-eyed peas for luck the next day
rituals: Counting down with the ball drop on TV.
Everyone writes one resolution and reads it out a year later.
Pots and pans on the porch at midnight.
Home before 1 because nobody wants the traffic.

dishes: carrot cake with cream cheese frosting
rituals: An egg hunt in the backyard, even for the adults.
Church in the morning and brunch after.
Dyeing eggs at the kitchen table the night before.
A basket of candy that nobody admits they still want.

dishes: burgers and hot dogs on the grill
potato salad from the family recipe
corn on the cob with too much butter
a flag cake with blueberries and strawberries
rituals: Fireworks from the same spot every year.
Lawn chairs set up hours early for the parade.
A backyard cookout that runs until dark.
Sparklers once it gets dark enough.

dishes: a cake from the good bakery
rituals: Brunch out, booked weeks ahead.
A long phone call, even from out of town.
Flowers from the farmers market.

dishes: a slice of key lime pie
rituals: An afternoon at a ballgame.
A round of mini golf that gets serious.
A long phone call, even from out of town.

dishes: grilled sausages with peppers and onions
rituals: One last cookout before summer is over.
A day at the lake with the whole family.

dishes: roast turkey with pigs in blankets
Christmas pudding set alight with brandy
roast potatoes done in goose fat
brussels sprouts that one person actually likes
a tin of chocolates on the coffee table
rituals: Crackers pulled at the table and paper crowns worn all afternoon.
The King's speech at three o'clock.
A walk after lunch whatever the weather.
A family argument over the board game, every single year.

dishes: a curry from the same takeaway
rituals: A carol service by candlelight.
A mince pie and a carrot left out by the fire.
A Christmas film nobody can agree on.

dishes: bubble and squeak from the leftovers
rituals: A long muddy walk.
The football on in the afternoon.
Visiting the other side of the family.

dishes: hot cross buns toasted with butter
rituals: An egg hunt in the garden.
Easter eggs from every relative.
Church in the morning and a roast after.

dishes: a Sunday roast out at a pub
breakfast in bed, slightly burnt toast
rituals: Flowers and a card delivered in person.
A long phone call, even from out of town.
The big bonfire and fireworks in the park.
Sparklers in the back garden.

dishes: a buffet of crisps and sausage rolls
rituals: Watching the fireworks over the Thames on telly.
Auld Lang Syne in a circle, arms crossed.
A pancake-flipping contest that always ends on the floor.
Sebae bows to the elders, and envelopes of new bills after.
A long drive to the hometown in holiday traffic.
Yunnori on the floor after lunch.
Charye, the ancestral table, set early in the morning.

dishes: pears and persimmons from the market
rituals: Making songpyeon together the night before.
A visit to the grandparents' graves to tidy them.
Gift sets of Spam or pears traded between relatives.
Everyone looks at the full moon and makes a wish.

dishes: a cake from the bakery downstairs
rituals: Red carnations pinned on the parents.
A long phone call, even from out of town.

dishes: a Christmas cake from the bakery
rituals: Lights at the department store plazas.
A small gift exchange with friends.
Watching the Bosingak bell ring on TV.
Staying up for the first sunrise.
Hatsumode, the first shrine visit, in a long line.
Otoshidama envelopes for the younger ones.
Nengajo cards read out at the table.
The whole family dozes at the kotatsu all afternoon.
The Kohaku song contest on TV.
The temple bell rung 108 times at midnight.
The big clean of the house, the oosouji, done in the morning.

dishes: cucumber horse and eggplant cow on the altar
rituals: A trip back to the hometown on a packed train.
Lanterns hung to welcome the ancestors home.
Bon odori dancing in the evening.
Cleaning the family grave together.

dishes: a bucket of fried chicken, ordered weeks ahead
rituals: A night out to see the illuminations.
A small gift exchange.

dishes: an ehomaki roll eaten in silence facing the lucky direction
rituals: Mamemaki, throwing beans out the door for luck.
Koinobori carp streamers flying from the balcony.

dishes: a roast turkey with oyster dressing
rituals: Grace said long enough that the food goes cold.
The whole family crowds into the parlor after dinner.
A football game in the afternoon, or at least the scores in the paper.
Carols around the piano.
Stockings hung by the fireplace.
Church in the morning in their best clothes.

dishes: fried chicken in a picnic basket
peach ice cream turned by hand
rituals: A picnic in the park and the band concert.
Firecrackers set off in the street.
The Easter parade in new hats.
Church in the morning, dinner after.

dishes: punch that is not entirely lemonade
rituals: A dance with a band until well past midnight.
Noisemakers and paper hats at the stroke of twelve.

dishes: roast goose with sage and onion
Christmas pudding with a sixpence inside
rituals: Stir-up Sunday, when everyone stirs the pudding and makes a wish.
Parlour games after dinner, snapdragon included.
Carols by the fire.
Crackers pulled at the table.
Christmas boxes for the tradespeople.
A long walk in the cold.
Church in their best and a family dinner after.
The guy paraded through the street and onto the bonfire.
A pancake race down the lane.
The quarter day reckoning of rents and wages, then supper.

dishes: a boar roasted on the spit
mince pies shaped like a manger
rituals: The Yule log dragged in and kept burning for twelve days.
Mummers coming to the door.
Mass at midnight and feasting after.

dishes: the Twelfth cake with a bean baked inside
rituals: Whoever finds the bean is king for the night.
Wassailing the apple trees.

dishes: a lamb roasted for the day
rituals: Creeping to the cross and then feasting.
Bonfires on the hill until dawn.
Birch and fennel hung over the door.

dishes: the first loaf from the new wheat
rituals: The first loaf taken to be blessed.

dishes: a goose fattened on the stubble
rituals: Rents paid and the harvest reckoned, then a goose supper.
The winter slaughter and a feast before the lean months.

dishes: pancakes and fritters to use up the eggs
rituals: A football game through the village streets.
